chapter: Corrections and views on early Black music
title: Honorable service record and later invitations to rejoin Army bands
summary: White cites his citation letter and offers to have joined regular Army bands, including one at Fort Huachuca.

story.theme_name: Drafted: musicians in the military and the war years
story.community_name: Drafted: service bands, USO shows and the war years

blocks.x: I never had a committed an offense except not having my card with me. Card with me, yeah. And that's been claimed by the War Department and the United States Army even while I was in the service.
Certainly you wouldn't have been in the service.

And now I hold a, not only a citation of honorable merit of the service, but a citation letter from my colonel. And the letter reads, a very valuable soldier to the United States Army. My best wishes go with you and I hope you will make a career of the service. And I could have made a career of the service because at that time there were four regular organized Negro regiments and I could have gone to any one of the bands at the request of their then band masters. And as early as the breakout of World War II, I was asked to come back down to Fort Huachuca and join the band which now is being conducted by, by Crawford in Germany. Crawford was the first chair trumpet player and Mr. Hammond was the band master. And Mr. Hammond passed in Phoenix, Arizona here last year, this year. And Mr. Hammond asked me to come back to the band and he was one of the most discriminating band masters the United States Army ever had.
